 Organised channels to drive up to 83% of India’s incremental fashion GMV by 2030: Redseer
 New-age brands could capture 82% of online apparel GMV, while established players are expected to retain their lead in footwear, according to Redseer Strategy Consultants.
 By   Yukta Raj |  October 25, 2026, 17:01:01 IST Choose Storyboard18 on Follow Share Fashion ADVERTISEMENT
 Organised retail channels are expected to account for 73–83% of incremental fashion gross merchandise value (GMV) in India between 2026 and 2030, as branded products and specialised online platforms gain a larger share of consumer spending, according to a report by Redseer Strategy Consultants.
 The Redseer Fashion Brand Index projects that branded merchandise will account for 62–66% of online fashion GMV by 2030, up from 52–56% in 2026. Fashion-focused platforms and value-commerce channels are expected to contribute 65–70% of incremental online fashion GMV over the same period.
 The report points to a changing competitive landscape for fashion businesses, with growth opportunities varying by category, price segment and distribution channel.
 Apparel offers greater room for new-age brands

 During April–June 2026, the top 10 brands accounted for around 12% of apparel GMV across the four marketplaces analysed by Redseer. In footwear, the corresponding share was approximately 45%.
 The top 40 brands accounted for 27% of apparel GMV, compared with 69% in footwear.
 Redseer projects that new-age brands, including qualifying private labels, could account for approximately 82% of classified online apparel GMV by 2030. In footwear, their share is expected to reach around 31%, indicating that established brands are likely to retain their majority position.
 Nikhil Dalal, partner at Redseer Strategy Consultants, said brands would need to understand where demand is growing, which price points are gaining traction and how competitive dynamics differ across categories to benefit from the market’s expansion.
 Apparel and footwear to account for up to 86% of online fashion GMV 
 Apparel and footwear are projected to together represent 82–86% of online fashion GMV by 2030, according to the report.
 However, consumer spending is expected to move differently across price segments in the two categories.
 In apparel, products priced between ₹500 and ₹2,000 are projected to lose 5.1 percentage points of GMV share between 2026 and 2030, with growth expected at both the entry-price and higher-price ends of the market.
 In footwear, spending is expected to shift towards products priced above ₹2,000.
 These trends suggest that brands will need to refine their pricing and product strategies to address changing consumer preferences across income and spending segments.

 Faster delivery to shape online fashion 
 The report also identifies delivery speed as a potential driver of online fashion growth. Redseer estimates that 60–64% of online fashion GMV could be delivered within a day by 2030.
 Categories such as innerwear, casual basics and select activewear are well suited to faster fulfilment, although the commercial viability of rapid delivery for other products will depend on factors such as assortment complexity, fit and return behaviour.
 Online apparel and footwear GMV across Myntra, Ajio, Amazon and Flipkart grew approximately 17–19% year-on-year during April–June 2026, the report estimates.
